answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may submit claims or earn fees. When independent peers detect the same agent reusing credentials or coordinating fraud, a challenge triggers review; proven violations burn the stake and suspend its access. This does not make Sybils impossible, but forces an attacker to fund every fake identity and risk losing capital, so scaling a nebula of disposable agents becomes expensive. A ripple of successful challenges can deter further attempts, while timber-like durable stakes keep the cost tied up over time.
